title: The Missing Practice Dispatch
setting: A volunteer hall during an announced training exercise
pressure: A short, unscored rehearsal: find the moved envelope and support your first group vote.
opening: You are leading an announced training exercise at a volunteer hall. A blue practice dispatch envelope has left its tray. Nobody is missing or hurt; the case and its watches are a simulation.

Six volunteers have signed accounts. One has secretly been assigned to move the envelope and conceal the route: this is the Mafia role used by the game controls. A Doctor can protect a witness during a watch, and your Detective team can check one person at night.

Begin with the accounts, ask one witness one selected question, then inspect the collection sheet. A comparison needs recorded sources. You can ask the group to Suspect someone, but the final vote is a separate action.

cast.name: Theo
cast.description: Theo folds the last chair and leaves the walkway clear.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: I stayed by the front doors while the practice envelope was being moved. Mara was sorting at the dispatch table.
cast.observation: There are two trays on the dispatch table. One is for arrival, the other for collection. Neither tray is locked.
cast.secret: I counted one stack of chairs twice on the setup sheet. I will correct the total before the hall opens.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: I could see the dispatch table, but I was carrying chairs. I was not watching every hand.

cast.name: Mara
cast.description: Mara leaves a space on the table where the blue envelope had been.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: The blue practice envelope was in the dispatch tray before I moved the chairs. I returned to the same table.
cast.observation: I saw Ellis lift the blue practice envelope from Dispatch and carry it into the supply room. I saw his face. I did not see him bring it back.
cast.secret: I left my sorting station briefly without asking for cover. I wanted to finish the chairs before anyone noticed the delay.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: I saw the envelope being carried into the supply room. I did not look inside the envelope or follow Ellis through the door.

cast.name: Ellis
cast.description: Ellis straightens the welcome cards while the others check the empty tray.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: I stayed at the welcome desk after setup. I did not handle the blue practice envelope.
cast.observation: The supply room is shared. Finding something there would not mean only one person could have put it there.
cast.secret: I asked to try the hidden saboteur part in a future exercise. That request does not tell you who was assigned it today.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: I went through the supply doorway during setup. Saying I stayed at the desk was too broad. Check the collection sheet before deciding what I carried.

cast.name: June
cast.description: June checks the practice watch list beside a closed first-aid kit.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: I was at the first-aid table during the dispatch exercise. No one has been hurt. Theo was moving chairs by the entrance.
cast.observation: The watch list assigns protection for the exercise. It is a game procedure, not a report of an injury.
cast.secret: I forgot to initial the kit checklist before we began. The kit was checked; the missing initial is mine.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: I saw Theo by the entrance several times. I cannot turn those glimpses into an uninterrupted watch.

cast.name: Noah
cast.description: Noah keeps the supply cupboard open so its shelves can be checked together.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: I prepared the supply shelves before the exercise, then joined June at the first-aid table.
cast.observation: The collection shelf was empty at setup. After the exercise began I saw Ellis place a blue envelope on it, behind the folded sign.
cast.secret: I used the wrong shelf label yesterday and corrected it this morning. Today’s shelf photograph shows the corrected arrangement.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: I saw Ellis put a blue envelope on the collection shelf. The dispatch number, rather than its color alone, should identify it.

cast.name: Priya
cast.description: Priya clips the collection sheet to a board without filling in any missing lines.
cast.relationship: A volunteer in the hall’s announced dispatch exercise.
cast.account: I kept the dispatch sheet at the table. Each volunteer signed for anything they collected. The practice envelope was marked D-4.
cast.observation: The collection sheet has a return column as well as a collection column. An empty return line should not be silently filled from memory.
cast.secret: I misspelled a name on yesterday’s sheet and recopied it. I kept both pages so the correction could be checked.
cast.defense: Keep what I saw beside what the dispatch sheet records.
cast.correction: My sheet records a signed collection. Mara’s sighting is the independent check on who actually carried the envelope.

connections.speaker: priya
connections.subject: ellis
connections.text: Ellis says he never handled the envelope. Mara saw him take it into Supply, and the collection sheet carries his signature for D-4 with no return. That gives us a supported case to discuss.
connections.reply: The sheet and the sighting need an answer. I cannot use a busy desk to account for an envelope I signed for.

connections.speaker: noah
connections.subject: ellis
connections.text: The setup photograph shows an empty shelf. My sighting puts the envelope there in Ellis’s hands afterward. That is a second check on the journey missing from his account.
connections.reply: The photograph fixes the starting point. I need to explain the movement after it, not just who could use the room.

timeline: Before the exercise, Priya marks the blue dispatch D-4 and Noah photographs an empty collection shelf.
The exercise facilitator privately assigns Ellis the saboteur role and June the Doctor role.
Ellis signs D-4 out from the dispatch tray while Mara is returning from the chairs.
Mara sees Ellis carry the envelope into Supply; Noah sees him set it behind the folded sign.
Ellis leaves the return column blank and gives an account denying that he handled the envelope.
The Detective team compares the signed collection with Mara’s observation before the practice ballot.
solution: Ellis moved the practice dispatch D-4 into the supply room as the assigned saboteur. His signature and Mara’s direct sighting contradict his claim that he did not handle it. This was an exercise; no real crime or death occurred.
chapters: Read the accounts before choosing one question. Mara was beside the dispatch route; the collection sheet can provide an independent check.
ending_win: The group identifies the assigned saboteur and returns D-4 to its tray. The exercise ends with the envelope, the signed sheet, and the witness’s limits kept together. Your practice result does not affect scores.
ending_loss: The exercise is stopped and the assigned route is explained. The envelope returns to its tray. You can rehearse again; this practice result does not affect scores.
reconstruction: Ellis was assigned the hidden saboteur role for this announced exercise. He signed D-4 out, carried it into Supply, and placed it behind a folded sign.
Mara’s detail answer provides a direct sighting. The dispatch sheet provides an independent signed collection with no return. Together they contradict Ellis’s initial account.

A supported comparison adds public reasons for suspicion. Asking the group to Suspect adds the team’s position; it does not cast a ballot or guarantee a result. The Detective team still needs to vote.

incidents.night: {name} leaves this practice watch and waits with the facilitator. Nobody is hurt; the dispatch exercise continues with the recorded accounts.
incidents.vote: {name} steps out of the exercise under the facilitator’s supervision. The collection sheet stays on the dispatch table for the practice verdict.
incidents.rescue: {name} stays in the exercise after a protected watch. Nobody is hurt; the blue dispatch remains the question at the table.

complexity.label: Very easy
